title: Spectral Weyl Spaces and Corrected Orthogonality in KdV Theory
content: This paper develops a mathematically rigorous framework for studying the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation through spectral theory and quantum neural network approximations. We introduce spectral Weyl spaces $\mathcal{W}^s_{u_0}$ — genuine Hilbert spaces attached to a fixed reference potential $u_0$ — that incorporate the discrete spectral data of the associated Schrödinger operator. Unlike previous formulations where the norm depended nonlinearly on the function being measured, our definition fixes the spectral data of the initial datum $u_0$ as a parameter, ensuring linearity and completeness. Our contributions are threefold. First, we establish global well-posedness of the KdV equation for $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb{R})$, $s>1/2$, with a polynomial growth estimate for the $H^s$-norm involving the spectral functional $\mathfrak{S}(u_0)=\sum_j(1+|\lambda_j|)^s$, where $\{\lambda_j\}$ are the negative eigenvalues of the Lax operator. While global existence is rigorously proved, the sharp polynomial rate with the exact spectral constant remains an open problem requiring a full $I$-method analysis, and is presented as a working hypothesis. Second, we construct a quantum neural network operator (QNNO) that formally approximates finite-dimensional truncations of the KdV flow, providing an asymptotic expansion with three layers: integer powers from Fr\'echet derivatives, fractional powers from truncated Marchaud derivatives (correctly defined on bounded parameter ranges), and quantum commutator terms arising from non-commutativity in the Lax pair. Third, we develop a multi-scale spectral decomposition into solitonic, intermediate, and radiative components, establishing exact $L^2$-orthogonality and an explicit quasi-orthogonality estimate in $H^s$ with a commutator error term — correcting a previous erroneous claim of exact $H^s$-orthogonality. Throughout, we clearly distinguish rigorously proved results from conjectural extensions, replacing unverified external citations with self-contained arguments or explicitly labeled open problems.
